title: N5 sentence patterns with build and typing sentences

forms.name: A is not B
forms.note: ではありません is the polite negative of です. In casual speech it becomes じゃない.
forms.trap: Do not say ないです after a noun in polite speech: it is ではありません.
ex: 私は先生ではありません。
これは私の本ではありません。

forms.name: A is (い-adjective)
forms.note: An い-adjective ends in い. Add です to be polite: このカレーは辛いです.
forms.trap: Do not put だ or の between the adjective and です.
ex: このカレーは辛いです。

forms.name: A is (な-adjective)
forms.note: A な-adjective takes です directly: 静かです. Before a noun it adds な: 静かな町.
forms.trap: Do not add い or な before です: 静かです, not 静かなです.

forms.name: Was (past of です)
forms.note: でした is the past of です. The past negative is ではありませんでした.
forms.trap: There is no separate past form for the noun itself: only です changes.

forms.name: Did (past of ます)
forms.note: ました is the past of ます and ませんでした is the past negative.
forms.trap: Do not use the plain past た in polite speech.
ex: 朝ご飯を食べませんでした。

forms.name: Asking a question
forms.note: Add か to the end of a polite sentence to ask a question. The word order does not change.
forms.trap: Do not move the verb to the front as in English: only add か.

forms.name: A の B
forms.note: の links two nouns. A の B can mean B belongs to A, or B is of the kind A.
forms.trap: Japanese puts the owner first: 私の本, not 本の私.

forms.name: From … to …
forms.note: から marks the starting point and まで marks the end, for time and for place.
forms.trap: Do not use に for both ends: から … まで.
ex: 九時から五時まで働きます。
I work from nine to five.
家から駅まで歩きます。
I walk from home to the station.

forms.name: Do something with someone
forms.note: と marks the person you do something with.
forms.trap: Do not use に for the companion: 友達と行きます.
ex: I watch a movie with a friend.
母と買い物に行きます。
I go shopping with my mother.

forms.name: Also (も)
forms.note: も replaces は, が or を and means “also”.
forms.trap: Do not keep は or を next to も: 私も学生です.
ex: My older brother reads books too.

forms.name: There is a person or animal
forms.note: います is used for people and animals, あります for things.
forms.trap: Do not use あります for a cat or a person.
ex: There is a cat in the room.
There are children in the park.

forms.name: Do something at a time
forms.note: に marks a point in time: 七時に起きます. Words like 今日 and 明日 take no に.
forms.trap: Do not add に after 今日, 明日 or 毎日.
ex: 日曜日に公園へ行きます。
I go to the park on Sunday.

forms.name: Do not (ません)
forms.note: ません is the polite negative of ます.
forms.trap: Do not use ない in polite speech.
ex: 今日は学校へ行きません。
I do not go to school today.

forms.name: Let's / Shall we?
forms.note: ましょう means “let's” and ませんか is a gentle invitation.
forms.trap: Do not use ましょう to refuse; it only invites.
ex: 明日、映画を見ませんか。
Shall we watch a movie tomorrow?

forms.name: A is more … than B
forms.note: より marks the thing compared with: AはBより大きいです.
forms.trap: Do not say もっと before the adjective unless you want “even more”.
ex: 兄は私より背が高いです。
My older brother is taller than me.
電車はバスより速いです。
The train is faster than the bus.

forms.name: The most …
forms.note: 一番 means “number one”: 一番高い is the tallest or most expensive.
forms.trap: Do not use より for the superlative.
ex: 果物の中でりんごが一番好きです。
Of the fruits, I like apples the best.
日本で富士山が一番高いです。
Mt. Fuji is the highest in Japan.

forms.name: Like or dislike something
forms.note: The thing you like takes が, not を: 音楽が好きです.
forms.trap: Do not use を with 好き or 嫌い.

forms.name: Want something
forms.note: 欲しい is an い-adjective. The thing you want takes が.
forms.trap: Do not use ほしい for a third person's wish without 〜がる.
ex: 私は新しいかばんが欲しいです。
私は時間が欲しいです。

forms.name: Can do (ability)
forms.note: できます means can do. The thing you can do takes が: 日本語ができます.
forms.trap: Do not use を with できます.
ex: 私は日本語ができます。
兄はスキーができます。

forms.name: Number + counter
forms.note: The number and counter come right before the verb: りんごを三つ買います.
forms.trap: Do not put the number before the object as in English: 三つりんごを is unnatural.
ex: りんごを三つ買いました。

forms.name: This / that / that over there
forms.note: これ is near me, それ near you, あれ far from both. Before a noun use この, その, あの.
forms.trap: Do not use これ before a noun: この本, not これ本.

forms.name: Where something is
forms.note: Position words follow の: 机の上, 駅の前, かばんの中.
forms.trap: Do not put the position word before の: 上の机 means “the desk above”.
ex: 机の上に本があります。
There is a book on the desk.
駅の前に銀行があります。
There is a bank in front of the station.
